answer: One defense is concurrency-priced admission: the contract prices signups at fee = 0.002 x P x n, where P is the epoch reward pool and n the identities live then. A lone entrant on a tundra-thin market pays little, but k simultaneous signups cross-price each other: clone k pays 0.002P x k, so k clones cost about 0.001P x k^2. Validators forge this rule into the opcode and reject underpriced txs. The bound variable is the global active count at signing: attackers cannot reset or split it, since each clone raises n for every clone in one umber-timed window. So cost tracks n.
